S68.01.needs: a signed-in account and a second client
S68.01.note: The session ID is only visible in the URL; no button shows it.
steps: Sign in, open Code and open a cloud session
Copy the address from the address bar (it ends in the session ID)
Open the same address in a second signed-in browser or client
Compare the session title and transcript with the first client
S68.01.where: Address bar of a Code session page, /code/<sessionId>

S68.02.needs: a Free or paid account with an existing Code session
S68.02.note: The exact text of the session list entry was not located; the path starts at the Code surface.
steps: Open a cloud session that already has turns
Read the transcript from the first message down
Open the same session on a second client and compare the transcript
S68.02.where: Code > open a session (address /code/<sessionId>), read the transcript

S68.03.needs: a session linked to a repository
steps: Open a cloud session that is linked to a repository
Click the Changes button in the session header
Read the branch line at the top of the panel (base, arrow, working branch)
Compare the working branch name on a second client
S68.03.where: Code session page > Changes (header button) > branch line at the top of the panel

S68.04.needs: a session linked to a repository
S68.04.note: The chip text is built from the environment and repository name, so no fixed label exists in the code.
steps: Open a cloud session linked to a repository
Read the chip beside the title (environment, then a dot, then repository)
Open the same session on a second client and compare the chip
S68.04.where: Code session page > header chip beside the session title

S68.06.needs: a paid account with Code sessions
S68.06.note: Gate in apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts only decides whether sandbox execution is enabled (AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY); no visible model or instruction-file setting was found for each client.

S68.08.needs: a Code session that reaches an approval step (needs the sandbox gate switched on)
S68.08.note: The cloud button label is built from the shared approve label plus 'and continue'; the literal 'Approve and continue' is from the local copy. Pending approval depends on the unfinished sandbox switch-on.
steps: Start a task in a cloud session that needs a tool approval
Wait for the Approval required card in the transcript
Read the approval reason and the command shown in the card
Click Approve and continue or Deny
Open the same session on a second client and check the card is answered there
S68.08.where: Code session page > transcript > Approval required card > Deny or Approve and continue

S68.09.needs: a Code session with a task that uses tools (sandbox gate switched on)
S68.09.note: Tool activity is shown in the transcript; no separate tool-activity panel was found.
steps: Send a task in a Code session
Watch the transcript while the task runs
Note the tool steps as they appear
Open the same session on a second client and compare the tool steps
S68.09.where: Code session page > send a task > transcript while the turn runs

S68.11.needs: a Code session that is running a turn (sandbox gate switched on for approvals)
S68.11.note: The approvals route moved; the UI reads approvals in apps/web/features/code/components/CodeTranscript.tsx.
steps: Open a running cloud session
Send a new turn from the composer
Click Stop the task while the turn runs
When an Approval required card appears, click Approve and continue or Deny
Check the result on the same session in a second client
S68.11.where: Code session page > composer (send a turn) > Stop the task while running > Approval required card

S68.13.note: Searched apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts and CodeChangesPanel.tsx for transfer and found no transfer-control text; the nearest is the Continue in VS Code link, which is not an explicit handoff.

S68.15.needs: the Desktop app and a cloud session
S68.15.note: Only help text exists (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts line 325 says a session can be continued in the desktop app); no button to continue a cloud session on Desktop was found, and the sandbox gate is unfinished.

S68.17.needs: a session linked to a repository with changes
S68.17.note: These are the nearest controls that return results; no control was found that names the local workspace directly.
steps: Open a cloud session that has changed files
Click the Changes button in the session header
Review the changed files and click Create pull request, or click Continue in VS Code
Check the pull request or the editor shows the cloud results
S68.17.where: Code session page > Changes (header button) > Create pull request, or Continue in VS Code

S68.19.needs: a Desktop app linked to the account
S68.19.note: Where the Your computer link appears in the navigation was not verified.
steps: Sign in and open the Your computer link, or type /code/computer in the address bar
Read the heading and the Computers on your account list
Check each computer shows its name and presence (online, asleep or offline)
S68.19.where: Your computer (link named 'Your computer') > /code/computer > section Computers on your account

S68.20.needs: a linked device on the account
S68.20.note: Rows are shown as list rows; the page does not show a card.
steps: Open Settings and choose Account
Scroll to Linked devices
Read each device row for its name, platform, surface and status (Online, Sleeping or Offline)

S68.21.needs: a linked device that reports capabilities
S68.21.note: The list has no Code sessions item, which the Expected line names; the cited dispatcher.ts line does not show capabilities.
steps: Open Settings, then Account, then Linked devices
Read the capability names under a device (Browser, Computer use, Local models, Local MCP, Remote Control)
Compare the list with what that machine runs
S68.21.where: Settings > Account > Linked devices > capability names under a device

S68.22.needs: the Desktop app on a computer and a browser
S68.22.note: The Desktop menu path was written in the web page copy only; 'Pair a phone' was not found in apps/desktop/src or packages/ui. The 503 'Pairing is not configured' check is unfinished until the website deploy.
steps: Open /code/computer in a signed-in browser
In the Desktop app, copy the pairing link for a browser (the page text says: Settings, Capabilities, Remote Control, Pair a phone, then Copy link for a browser)
Paste the link into the field labelled Pairing link
Click Connect and read the status
Check the computer shows as connected
S68.22.where: /code/computer > Pairing link field > Connect (paste the link copied in the Desktop app)

steps: Pair a computer as in S68.22 and open /code/computer
Click Disconnect and read the confirm dialog
Confirm and check the page shows the connection has ended
Try to send a task again and check it stops working
Or open Settings > Account > Linked devices and click Unlink, then confirm
S68.23.where: /code/computer > Disconnect (confirm Disconnect from your computer?) ; or Settings > Account > Linked devices > Unlink

labels.text: Your computer went offline. This page reconnects when it is back.

S68.25.needs: a paired computer that you can take offline
S68.25.note: Linked devices shows the word Offline only, with no explanation; the explanation is on /code/computer.
steps: Pair with a computer and open /code/computer
Quit the Desktop app or put the computer to sleep
Read the message on the page
Open Settings > Account > Linked devices and read the presence label for that device
S68.25.where: /code/computer > message below Connecting (shown when the computer goes offline)
